parts.text: An isotope of boron is used in the treatment of cancer in the brain. Boron sticks to cancer cells in the brain.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The isotope of boron is bombarded with neutrons then undergoes fission to form lithium and alpha‑particles.

ms.label: 8(a)(i)
ms.text:
fission is splitting of nuclei
OR
fusion is the joining of nuclei

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) A nucleus of boron (B) contains 5 protons and 5 neutrons. Complete the nuclide equation for this fission reaction. ......... ......... B + 1 0 n ......... ......... Li + ......... ......... α [3]

Li: proton number 3 and nucleon number 7

ms.label: 8(b)
ms.text:
alpha is less penetrating / has shorter range (than gamma)
alpha more easily absorbed / stopped by cancer / tumour cells or won’t travel beyond cancer cells or so won’t damage
other / healthy cells
OR
alpha highly ionising (than gamma)
will destroy / damage cancer cells more easily

ms.label: 8(c)
ms.text:
any one from:
•
reduce exposure time
•
increase distance between source and living tissue or stand in another room whilst radiation is emitted
•
use shielding or wear a lead apron or stand behind a glass partition / lead barrier
